div.head: I Cn 26.2
div.ab: Nis nan swa yfel sceaða, swa is deofol sylf: he byð á ymbe þæt an, hu he on manna saulum mæst gesceaðian mæge.
Nis nan swa yfel sceaða, swa is deofol sylf: he bið a ymbe þæt án, hu he mæge on mannum sawlum mæst gesceaðian.
Nis nan swa yfel sceaða, swa is deofol sylf: he bið á ymbe þæt an, hu he on mannum sawlum mæst gesceaðian mæge.
Non est aliquis tam nocens aduersarius sicut accusator humani generis inimicus, qui totis semper uisceribus inhiat, totis estuat desideriis, quomodo plures animas pertrahat in supplicium.
Set nullus latro tam nocens ut diabolus, qui semper circa hoc satagit, qualiter in animabus hominum maxime latrocinari possit.
Nis nan swa yfel sceaða swa is deofol sylf; he bið a ymbe þæt án, hu he mæge on mannum sawlum mæst gesceaðian.
Nis nan swa yfel sceaða swa is deofol sylf; he byð a ymbe þæt an, hu he on mannum saulum mæst gesceaðian mæge.
Es lebt kein so schlimmer Verderber, wie der Teufel selbst ist: er ist immer um das Eine bemüht, wie er unter Menschenseelen (Menschen den Seelen B A) am meisten schaden könne.
There is no robber so evil as the devil himself: he is always intent on one thing, how he can do most harm among men's souls (to men in their souls, B A).
There is no spoiler so evil as is the devil himself; he is ever concerned with one thing only, namely, how he can do most harm to the souls of men.
There is no predator so evil as the devil himself; he is always concerned with only one thing, how he can best prey upon people’s souls.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 307, October 2026 (MS Cons)
